title: High dev fixture: exhaustive review format and styling stress test

behaviorFlow.label: User invokes dev command
behaviorFlow.description: The user runs /pr-dev or the CLI dev-render command with familiar output/detail flags.

behaviorFlow.label: Fixture data loads
behaviorFlow.description: The CLI loads static report JSON and a static GitSnapshot fixture instead of reading real git state.

behaviorFlow.label: Renderer produces HTML
behaviorFlow.description: The normal chapters renderer writes one or more artifact HTML files for browser, responsive, and print review.

risks.description: The dev slash command runs a local CLI. Argument parsing and path handling must not accidentally invoke the review agent or inspect the wrong repository.
risks.mitigation: Keep /pr-dev on pi.exec only and route fixture rendering through dev-render.

risks.description: Long paths, commands, and diff lines can overflow narrow screens if tables or pre blocks are not constrained.
risks.mitigation: Use wrapping for prose/table cells and horizontal scroll for raw diffs.

risks.description: Fixtures can become stale when schema fields or renderer assumptions change.
risks.mitigation: Validate fixture report JSON on every dev-render run.

decisions.decision: Use fixture JSON plus fixture GitSnapshot instead of a bespoke HTML mock.
decisions.rationale: This keeps development rendering close to the production JSON-to-HTML workflow while avoiding model/token cost.
alternatives: Mock static HTML pages by hand
Require a real git repo with synthetic changes for every styling iteration

decisions.decision: Render all detail tiers from one command.
decisions.rationale: Ultralow omits raw diffs while high detail exercises dense risk, decision, and validation sections.
